summary.name: Redlamp
summary.one_liner: Redlamp is a native, open-source RAW photo editor for Apple Silicon Macs, built in Swift and Metal, aiming to keep Lightroom Classic's Develop workflow without a subscription or cloud.
use_cases: edit raw camera files on a Mac
replace Lightroom Classic for develop adjustments
batch or script raw processing via headless CLI
offline photo editing without a subscription
check color accuracy of raw rendering across camera files
summary.what_it_does: The page describes Redlamp as a native macOS RAW photo editor built from scratch in Swift and Metal, targeting Apple Silicon. It uses LibRaw, vendored as a pinned static XCFramework (arm64 only), to decode camera RAW files. The project includes an engine API contract, a headless CLI, and unit and engine smoke-test suites. Development infrastructure described includes GitHub Actions CI with purity and license-audit gates, a benchmark harness with recorded performance history, end-to-end regression tests, and golden-image color tests (ΔE2000) for camera files and bundled recipe versions. It is listed as open source on the awesome-mac list.
notable: Built from scratch in Swift and Metal with a clean-room policy
Headless CLI and engine API contract
Golden-image color regression tests using ΔE2000
Performance lab CI with regression gates that block merges
caveats: Targets Apple Silicon only (LibRaw built arm64 only)
iPhone and iPad support is planned for a later phase, not yet available
Page describes an early foundations phase; feature completeness versus Lightroom is not stated
